### 1. Interactive setup (recommended) {#interactive-setup}

On first run, the CLI starts a setup flow if it cannot find a key:

```bash
vibe
```

You can also rerun the setup at any time:

```bash
vibe --setup
```

The setup flow saves your key to `~/.vibe/.env` for future sessions.

text:
Now I have the complete picture. The documentation states there are three ways to provide the API key, listed in order of precedence:
1. Interactive setup (which saves to ~/.vibe/.env)
2. Environment variable (MISTRAL_API_KEY)
3. .env file (~/.vibe/.env)

And importantly: "Environment variables take precedence over values stored in `~/.vibe/.env`."

This means that when MISTRAL_API_KEY is exported as an environment variable, it takes precedence over the ~/.vibe/.env file (which is where a Vibe subscription would be stored after interactive setup).

So the answer is: the CLI uses the `MISTRAL_API_KEY` environment variable.

The user also wants me to cite the documentation. I need to provide the exact link format as specified in the instructions.

content.text:
The CLI uses the `MISTRAL_API_KEY` environment variable. Environment variables take precedence over values stored in `~/.vibe/.env` (where a Vibe subscription key from the setup wizard is stored).

[Environment variable](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/api-keys-profiles#env-var)
[.env file](https://docs.mistral.ai/vibe/code/cli/api-keys-profiles#env-file)
